title: WL-MT406-SurrealPromotionAndIndependentReadback
clause: Promote project-qualified local intents through one atomic SurrealDB domain-artifact-plus-EventLedger transaction and independently re-read canonical truth before acknowledging promotion locally.

conditional_execution.approved: Execute this contract normally after MT-405.
conditional_execution.rejected: Do not edit product code or create a promotion path; record validator-checked NOT_APPLICABLE_BY_MT401_REJECTION.

scope.summary: GOAL: Implement the only permitted local-to-canonical boundary. WpLocalStore may stage a project-qualified generic artifact/evidence/validation result intent with promotion_id, idempotency key, payload hash, canonical target and expected revision. Handshake then performs exactly one SurrealDB transaction that claims idempotency, writes the canonical artifact/result, appends the EventLedger event and advances the required head/revision. After commit, a separate request-scoped SurrealDB client independently re-reads the canonical record and event. Only a matching readback may mark the local intent promoted. This is not a distributed transaction, and local state can neither roll back nor override SurrealDB.
forbidden_paths: Direct local-to-domain writes outside the canonical SurrealDB repository
Marking promoted from local commit success or logs
Promotion of Notes, Loom, CKC, Tailor, Studio or canonical Locus payloads through WpLocalStore
Last-write-wins overwrite of newer canonical revisions
acceptance_criteria: Every intent requires promotion_id, idempotency_key, project_id, wp_id, allowed record_class, payload/artifact hash, canonical target, expected revision, actor, AccessSpace and source-scope hash; malformed or forbidden intents fail before either store mutates.
One SurrealDB transaction atomically writes the permitted canonical artifact/evidence/result, EventLedger append, idempotency claim and revision/head update; fault injection exposes all or none.

The transaction executes through the canonical typed SurrealDB repository with authenticated record-user/ResourceBroker authorization. WpLocalStore never receives a SurrealDB owner credential or raw repository bypass.

A fresh independent SurrealDB read after commit verifies project/WP scope, canonical record ID, event ID, hash, revision, actor and idempotency receipt. Local state is marked promoted only after all fields match.

If commit succeeds but readback or local acknowledgment fails, retry with the same idempotency key returns the existing canonical receipt and performs no second mutation/event; the local intent remains safely retryable.
If canonical revision advanced since staging, promotion fails with STALE_CANONICAL_PRECONDITION and preserves the local candidate for review; it cannot overwrite or merge automatically.
Promotion paths reject domain canonical content prohibited by MT-402/404, even when wrapped as generic artifacts or drafts.
proof_targets: Run real SurrealDB fault injection before/after idempotency claim, canonical write, EventLedger append, head update, commit, independent readback and local acknowledgment.
Repeat each crash point with the same promotion ID and prove exactly one canonical record/event and one stable receipt.
Use a separately constructed authenticated SurrealDB client for readback and prove it does not reuse transaction-local, cache or local-store state.
Race a staged intent against a newer canonical revision and prove fail-closed preservation without overwrite.
Attempt prohibited Notes/Loom/CKC/Tailor/Studio/Locus payload promotions and prove pre-transaction rejection.

gui_obligation.not_applicable_reason: Promotion engine is backend-only. MT-409 shows redacted pending/readback/stale/retry state and the canonical receipt link.

target_entries: WP-local working store > Promotion to SurrealDB
WP-local working store > Retry, stale state and independent verification

same_project_private_resource_cases: A same-project principal cannot promote or read back a target outside the source resource grant.
cross_account_negative_cases: Cross-project idempotency replay and target probing are denied without disclosing target existence.
derived_resource_non_widening_cases: The promoted resource scope is the intersection of source scopes and cannot be widened by intent metadata.
revocation_and_context_switch_cases: Revocation or AccessSpace switch before commit/readback fails closed and leaves the intent retryable but unacknowledged.
remote_saas_mcp_sync_cases: Promotion targets only the canonical Handshake SurrealDB repository and creates no remote Turso/MCP sync route.
metadata_side_channel_cases: Readback errors, receipt IDs, revisions and diagnostics do not reveal unauthorized target existence.

hbr_int_009_tier_obligations.reason: Promotion projects the canonical EventLedger receipt and local state transition with one correlation chain; Flight Recorder remains derived.
Stale precondition, commit/readback mismatch and retry posture require precise structured diagnostics.
Queued promotion/retry jobs expose bounded progress, cancellation and broker identity.

risk_if_missed: A split commit or local self-acknowledgment can claim promotion without canonical truth, duplicate EventLedger events, or overwrite newer SurrealDB state.

risks: The same repository/client or transaction response masquerades as independent readback.
Commit succeeds, local ack fails, and retry duplicates the event.
A generic artifact wrapper bypasses the domain denylist.
A stale local draft overwrites a newer canonical revision.
minimum_controls: Single SurrealDB transaction with idempotency and EventLedger.
Fresh authenticated independent readback before local ack.
Expected-revision compare-and-set and no automatic merge.
Pre-transaction domain record-class validation and crash matrix.

official_sources.title: SurrealDB manual transactions
official_sources.finding: Official Rust guidance supports multi-statement begin/commit/cancel transactions; canonical record, event, idempotency and head changes belong in one transaction.

official_sources.title: SurrealDB Rust begin method
official_sources.finding: The transaction handle provides commit and cancel semantics; readback after commit must use a separate request-scoped client path.

official_sources.title: Turso Rust SDK reference
official_sources.finding: Local transactions can durably stage intents, but they cannot participate atomically with SurrealDB; the protocol therefore uses idempotency and independent canonical verification.

research_provenance.selected_approach: Local stage, one canonical SurrealDB transaction, fresh independent SurrealDB readback, then local acknowledgment.
rejected_options: Domain content promotion through a generic wrapper
